$$ \displaystyle\int\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert h(x)-h_{\varepsilon}(x)}}\right\rvert\mu_{d}(dx) \displaystyle\leqslant C_{M}\sum_{1\leqslant i\leqslant K}\int\mathbf{1}_{[\alpha_{i}-\varepsilon,\alpha_{i}+\varepsilon]}(x)\mu_{d}(dx) \displaystyle=C_{M}\sum_{1\leqslant i\leqslant K}\int\mathbf{1}_{[\alpha_{i}-\varepsilon,\alpha_{i}+\varepsilon]}(x)\mu_{G}(dx)+\oo_{d}(1) \displaystyle\leqslant 2KC_{M}\varepsilon+\oo_{d}(1), $$

where in the second step we have applied the CLT, with the approximation error captured by $\oo_{d}(1)$ . Since $\varepsilon$ can be chosen to be arbitrarily small, we have established (A.6), about the unnormalized model. The estimate for the normalized model, (A.7), is the same, since it relies only on weak convergence of $\mu_{d}$ or $\widetilde{\mu_{d}}$ to $\mu_{G}$ .

Now we study the $e_{M}$ terms (A.8), (A.9), and (A.10). First we observe that, by construction,

$$ \mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert e_{M}(x)}}\right\rvert\leqslant C\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert^{C}\mathds{1}_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert\geqslant M} $$

for some $C$ , which can now change from line to line. Indeed, $e_{M}(x)$ agrees with $g^{2}(x)$ on $\{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert\geqslant M+1\}$ , where this growth rate is by assumption, and is constructed from $g$ and a linear interpolation on $\{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert\in[M,M+1]\}$ . From this, standard tail bounds give

$$ \mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\int_{\mathbb{R}}e_{M}(x)\mu_{G}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)}}\right\rvert\leqslant C\int_{M}^{\infty}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert^{C}\mu_{G}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)=\OO(e^{-M^{2}/4}), $$

which proves (A.8). Next, we combine the standard estimate

$$ \sup_{d}\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}}}\right)^{2p}}}\right]\leqslant C_{p} $$

with Cauchy–Schwartz and Markov’s inequality to find

$$ \begin{split}\int_{\mathbb{R}}e_{M}(x)\mu_{d}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)&\leqslant C\int_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert>M}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert^{C}\mu_{d}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)\leqslant 2\alpha_{1}^{2}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle/\sqrt{d}}}\right\rvert^{2C}}}\right]\mathbb{P}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle/\sqrt{d}}}\right\rvert>M}}\right)}}\right)^{1/2}\\
&\leqslant\frac{2\alpha_{1}^{2}}{M}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle/\sqrt{d}}}\right\rvert^{2C}}}\right]\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[(\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle/\sqrt{d})^{2}}}\right]}}\right)^{1/2}=\OO\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\frac{1}{M}}}\right),\end{split} $$

which verifies (A.9). Finally, we need to bound

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}}e_{M}(x)\widetilde{\mu_{d}}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)\leqslant C\int_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert>M}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert x}}\right\rvert^{C}\widetilde{\mu_{d}}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)=C\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{1}\|}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{2}\|}}}\right\rvert^{C}\mathds{1}_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{1}\|}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{2}\|}}}\right\rvert\geqslant M}}}\right]. $$

We will split this estimate into two parts, namely on and off the good event

$$ \mathcal{E}_{\textup{good}}=\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\{\|X_{1}\|\geqslant\frac{\sqrt{d}}{2}\text{ and }\|X_{2}\|\geqslant\frac{\sqrt{d}}{2}}}\right\}. $$

On this event,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{1}\|}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{2}\|}}}\right\rvert^{C}\mathds{1}_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{1}\|}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{2}\|}}}\right\rvert\geqslant M}\mathds{1}_{\mathcal{E}_{\textup{good}}}}}\right]\leqslant C\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}}}\right\rvert^{C}\mathds{1}_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}}}\right\rvert\geqslant\frac{M}{4}}}}\right], $$

which is $\OO(1/M)$ by the same arguments as in (A.12). On its complement, we apply the deterministic estimate $\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}}\right\rvert}{\|X_{1}\|\|X_{2}\|}\leqslant 1$ to find

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{1}\|}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{2}\|}}}\right\rvert^{C}\mathds{1}_{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\frac{\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\langle X_{1},X_{2}}}\right\rangle}{\sqrt{d}}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{1}\|}\frac{\sqrt{d}}{\|X_{2}\|}}}\right\rvert\geqslant M}\mathds{1}_{\mathcal{E}_{\textup{good}}^{c}}}}\right]\leqslant d^{C/2}\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\textup{good}}^{c}). $$

The estimate $\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left\lvert\|X\|-\sqrt{d}}}\right\rvert\prec 1$ from (9.6) gives $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\textup{good}}^{c})\leqslant C_{D}d^{-D}$ for any fixed $D>0$ ; if we take $D>C/2$ , we find that this is $\oo(1)$ as $d\to\infty$ . Thus $\limsup_{d\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}}e_{M}(x)\mu_{d}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x)=\OO(1/M)$ , which verifies (A.10) and finishes the proof. ∎
