$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle=\int_{|D_{11}|,|D_{22}|\leq N^{10}}|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle+\int_{|D_{11}|,|D_{22}|\geq N^{10}}|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle+\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}|D_{11}|\leq N^{10}\\
|D_{22}|\geq N^{10}\end{subarray}}|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle+\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}|D_{11}|\geq N^{10}\\
|D_{22}|\leq N^{10}\end{subarray}}|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle=\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{II}+\mathrm{III}+\mathrm{IV}. $$

Since $\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}$ is self-adjoint (as $\mathbf{H}$ is self-adjoint), we get that $|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|\geq 1$ . This implies $|\mathrm{I}|\leq N^{C}$ . Next, we note that

$$ \displaystyle|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-1/2} \displaystyle\leq|\det[\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]|^{-1/2} \displaystyle=|D_{11}|^{-\frac{N-2j+2}{2}}|D_{22}|^{-\frac{N-2j+2}{2}}|\det\mathbf{H}^{2}|^{-1/2} $$

for the same reason. But the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{H}^{2}$ are those of $H_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(\eta_{z,t})$ , which are uniformly $\gtrsim\theta_{j}^{2}$ by definition of $H_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(\eta_{z,t})$ and a bound on the operator norm of $A_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}$ of $\lesssim\theta_{j}^{-2}$ . This gives

$$ \displaystyle|\mathrm{II}| \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{|D_{11}|,|D_{22}|\geq N^{10}}|D_{11}|^{-\frac{N-2j+2}{2}}|D_{22}|^{-\frac{N-2j+2}{2}}\theta_{j}^{-2N}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle\lesssim C^{N}N^{-10(N-2j+6)}\theta_{j}^{-2N}. $$

We are left to bound $\mathrm{III}$ ; the bound for $\mathrm{IV}$ follows by the same argument but swapping $D_{11}$ and $D_{22}$ . For convenience, write

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{H}_{1}:=I+i\mathbf{H}\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&D_{22}\end{pmatrix}\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}. $$

We have

$$ \displaystyle|\det[I+i\mathbf{H}D\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}]| \displaystyle=|\det[\mathbf{H}_{1}]|\times\det\left[I+i\mathbf{H}_{1}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\mathbf{H}\begin{pmatrix}D_{11}&0\\
0&0\end{pmatrix}I_{N-2j+2}\mathbf{H}\mathbf{H}_{1}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right] \displaystyle\geq\left|\det\left[I+i\mathbf{H}^{2}\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&D_{22}\end{pmatrix}\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\right]\right|. $$

where the last inequality holds because the second factor in the second line has the form $|\det[I+iA]|$ with $A$ self-adjoint. Now, write $\mathbf{H}^{2}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{L}_{11}&\mathbf{L}_{12}\\ \mathbf{L}_{12}&\mathbf{L}_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ , and compute

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{H}^{2}\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&D_{22}\end{pmatrix}\otimes I_{N-2j+2} \displaystyle=D_{22}\begin{pmatrix}0&\mathbf{L}_{12}\\
0&\mathbf{L}_{22}\end{pmatrix}. $$

This gives us

$$ \displaystyle\left|\det\left[I+i\mathbf{H}^{2}\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&D_{22}\end{pmatrix}\otimes I_{N-2j+2}\right]\right|=\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&iD_{22}\mathbf{L}_{12}\\
0&1+iD_{22}\mathbf{L}_{22}\end{pmatrix}\right|\geq|\det[D_{22}\mathbf{L}_{22}]|. $$

Since $\mathbf{L}_{22}$ is a diagonal block of $\mathbf{H}^{2}$ , and since $\mathbf{H}$ is self-adjoint, we know that $\mathbf{L}_{22}$ is self-adjoint. We also recall $\mathbf{H}^{2}\gtrsim\theta_{j}^{2}$ from earlier in this proof. This implies $\mathbf{L}_{22}\gtrsim\theta_{j}^{2}$ by restricting to vectors in the block corresponding to $\mathbf{L}_{22}$ . Thus, the previous display is $\geq C^{-N}D_{22}^{N-2j+2}\theta_{j}^{-2N}$ . Ultimately,

$$ \displaystyle|\mathrm{III}| \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}|D_{11}\leq N^{10}\\
|D_{22}|\geq N^{10}\end{subarray}}|\det[D_{22}\mathbf{L}_{22}]|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_{11}-D_{22}|dD_{11}dD_{22} \displaystyle\lesssim N^{10}\int_{|D_{22}|\geq N^{10}}C^{N}D_{22}^{-\frac{N-2j+2}{2}}\theta_{j}^{-2N}dD_{22} \displaystyle\lesssim C^{N}N^{-5N+10j+12}\theta_{j}^{-2N}. $$

As mentioned earlier, the same bound holds for $\mathrm{IV}$ . This completes the proof. ∎

By the previous lemmas, we can now bound the integral $d\theta_{j}$ when $\theta_{j}\in\mathcal{I}_{1}$ .

#### Lemma 12.

Fix any $j\geq 1$ . There exists $\kappa>0$ such that locally uniformly in $a_{j},b_{j}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{I}_{1}}\frac{|\cos 2\theta_{j}|}{\sin^{2}2\theta_{j}}\psi_{j}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]\det[(A_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)})^{\ast}A_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\times\int_{M_{2}^{sa}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\det[I+i[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}]^{-\frac{1}{2}}dPd\theta_{j} \displaystyle\lesssim e^{-N^{\kappa}}. $$

We break up $\mathcal{I}_{1}=\mathcal{I}_{11}\cup\mathcal{I}_{12}$ , where $\mathcal{I}_{11}=[0,\frac{\pi}{4}-N^{-1/2+\tau}]$ and $\mathcal{I}_{12}=[\frac{\pi}{4}+N^{-1/2+\tau},\frac{\pi}{2}]$ . We will prove the estimate

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{I}_{11}}\frac{|\cos 2\theta_{j}|}{\sin^{2}2\theta_{j}}\psi_{j}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]\det[(A_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)})^{\ast}A_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\times\int_{M_{2}^{sa}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\det[I+i[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}]^{-\frac{1}{2}}dPd\theta_{j} \displaystyle\lesssim e^{-N^{\kappa}}. $$

The estimate for $\mathcal{I}_{12}$ instead of $\mathcal{I}_{11}$ follows by the same argument after changing variables $\theta_{j}\mapsto\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta_{j}$ .

By Lemmas 10 and 11, it suffices to show

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{I}_{11}}\frac{|\cos 2\theta_{j}|}{\sin^{2}2\theta_{j}}N^{C\epsilon_{0}}\exp\left\{-Cb_{j}^{2}N^{2}\eta_{z,t}^{2}[\tan\theta_{j}-\tan^{-1}\theta_{j}]^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\left[N^{C}+C^{N}N^{-10(N-2j+6)}\theta_{j}^{-2N}+N^{-5N+10j+12}\theta_{j}^{-2N}\right]d\theta_{j} \displaystyle\lesssim e^{-N^{\kappa}}. $$

Now, further decompose $\mathcal{I}_{11}=[0,c]\cup[c,\frac{\pi}{4}-N^{-1/2+\tau}]$ , where $c>0$ is a small, fixed constant.

Assume first that $\theta_{j}\in[c,\frac{\pi}{4}-N^{-1/2+\tau}]$ . We know $|\theta_{j}-\frac{\pi}{4}|\geq N^{-1/2+\tau}\eta_{z,t}^{-1}$ for $\tau>0$ small and fixed. Thus, the exponential in the first line in (3.3) is $O(\exp[-CN^{2\tau}])$ , and $|\cos 2\theta_{j}|^{-1}\lesssim N^{1/2}$ . So

$$ \displaystyle\int_{c}^{\frac{\pi}{4}-N^{-1/2+\tau}}\frac{|\cos 2\theta_{j}|}{\sin^{2}2\theta_{j}}N^{C\epsilon_{0}}\exp\left\{-Cb_{j}^{2}N^{2}\eta_{z,t}^{2}[\tan\theta_{j}-\tan^{-1}\theta_{j}]^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\left[N^{C}+C^{N}N^{-10(N-2j+6)}\theta_{j}^{-2N}+N^{-5N+10j+12}\theta_{j}^{-2N}\right]d\theta_{j} \displaystyle\lesssim D^{N}e^{-CN^{2\tau}}\lesssim e^{-N^{\kappa}}, $$

where $D=O(1)$ . We now handle the integral on $[0,c]$ . In this case, if $c>0$ is small enough, we have the lower bound $|\tan\theta_{j}-\tan^{-1}\theta_{j}|\gtrsim\theta_{j}^{-1}$ . We can also bound $|\cos 2\theta_{j}|=O(1)$ . Thus, we have the following estimate for $D=O(1)$ and $C>0$ :

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{c}\frac{|\cos 2\theta_{j}|}{\sin^{2}2\theta_{j}}N^{C\epsilon_{0}}\exp\left\{-Cb_{j}^{2}N^{2}\eta_{z,t}^{2}[\tan\theta_{j}-\tan^{-1}\theta_{j}]^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\left[N^{C}+C^{N}N^{-10(N-2j+6)}\theta_{j}^{-2N}+N^{-5N+10j+12}\theta_{j}^{-2N}\right]d\theta_{j} \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{0}^{c}\frac{1}{\sin^{2}2\theta_{j}}D^{N}\theta_{j}^{-2N}\exp[-Cb_{j}^{2}N^{2}\eta_{z,t}^{2}\theta_{j}^{-2}]d\theta_{j}. $$

But $N^{2}\eta_{z,t}^{2}\gg N$ since $\eta_{z,t}\gtrsim t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ . So, the exponential decays faster than $\theta_{j}^{-2N}$ or $\sin^{-2}2\theta_{j}$ blow up as $\theta_{j}\to 0$ . In particular, the last line is $\lesssim\exp[-N^{\kappa}]$ for some $\kappa>0$ by elementary calculus. This completes the proof. ∎

The goal of this section is to express every term above in terms of traces of resolvents.

### 4.1 Ratio of determinants

$$ \displaystyle\psi_{j}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}] \displaystyle=\det[(A^{(j-1)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(j-1)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}] \displaystyle\times\prod_{\ell=1}^{j-1}\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|^{-1}\left[1+O(N^{-\kappa})\right] $$

$$ \displaystyle m_{F}(r) \displaystyle:=\frac{e^{-\frac{rt}{2N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}F}}{K_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{t}\mathbf{v}^{\ast}\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}-\frac{rt}{N}F\right)\mathbf{v}\right\}d\mathbf{v} \displaystyle=\frac{e^{-\frac{rt}{2N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}F}e^{\frac{2N}{t}\eta_{z,t}^{2}}}{K_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{t}\mathbf{v}^{\ast}\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}-\frac{rt}{N}F\right)\mathbf{v}\right\}d\mathbf{v}, $$

where $K_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}$ is a normalizing constant chosen so that $m_{F}(0)=1$ . By Lemma 6, as in the proof of Lemma 7, we can compute

$$ \displaystyle\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{t}\mathbf{v}^{\ast}\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}-\frac{rt}{N}F\right)\mathbf{v}\right\}d\mathbf{v} \displaystyle=C_{N,t}\int_{M^{sa}_{2}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\left\{\det\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}-\frac{rt}{N}F+iP\otimes I_{N}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}}dP \displaystyle=C_{N,t}\left\{\det\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}-\frac{rt}{N}F\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\times\int_{M^{sa}_{2}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\left\{\det\left(1+\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(iP\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}}dP, $$

where $\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}:=(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}-\frac{rt}{N}F)^{-1}$ . Above, and throughout this proof, $C_{N,t}$ is a constant that comes from our application of Lemma 6; its exact value is not important. Next,

$$ \displaystyle\left\{\det\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}-\frac{rt}{N}F\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle=\left\{\det\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left\{\det\left(1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle=\left\{\det\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left(1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\}, $$

where $\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}:=\tilde{H}^{(0)}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}$ . Next, we compute

$$ \displaystyle\int_{M^{sa}_{2}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\left\{\det\left(1+\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(iP\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}}dP \displaystyle=\int_{M^{sa}_{2}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left(1+\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(iP\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)\right\}dP. $$

Putting all the previous displays together, we get

$$ \displaystyle m(r) \displaystyle=\frac{C_{N,t}e^{2\frac{N}{t}\eta_{z,t}^{2}}}{K_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\left\{\det\left(A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\ast}A_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}\right)\right\}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{rt}{2N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}F-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left(1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\} \displaystyle\times\int_{M^{sa}_{2}(\mathbb{R})}e^{i\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left(1+\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(iP\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)\right\}dP. $$

This identity can only hold if $1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}>0$ ; we will always have this condition for any $F$ we take. To control the second line, we have the following as in Lemma 6.2 of [23]:

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{rt}{2N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}F-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left(1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\} \displaystyle\lesssim\exp\left\{\frac{1}{\|1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{2}\right\}. $$

Let us now control the $dP$ integral in (4.2). Next, by Taylor expansion as in Section 6 of [23],

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left(1+\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(iP\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{i}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)^{2}+\mathcal{E}\right\}, $$

where $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies both $|e^{\mathcal{E}}|=O(1)$ and $|\mathcal{E}|\lesssim N\eta_{z,t}^{-6}\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{3}$ . Note that

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)} \displaystyle=\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\left(1-\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\frac{rt}{N}F\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{-1}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}. $$

Now, assume that $\|\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\frac{N^{\epsilon}}{N\eta_{z,t}^{3}}$ uniformly in $N$ . We will also always have this constraint, and it clearly implies $1-\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}>0$ if $\eta_{z,t}\gg N^{-\frac{1}{3}+\epsilon}$ . Next, we compute

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}={\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}(P\otimes I_{N}) \displaystyle={\operatorname{Tr}\,}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\left(1-\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\frac{rt}{N}F\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{-1}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N}) \displaystyle={\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}(P\otimes I_{N})+O\left(\frac{N^{\epsilon}}{\eta_{z,t}^{5}}\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right), $$

where the last line also uses $\|\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\eta_{z,t}^{-2}$ . By the same token, for some constant $C>0$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{CN^{\epsilon}}{\eta_{z,t}^{10}}\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{2}\right){\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq\left(1-\frac{CN^{\epsilon}}{\eta_{z,t}^{10}}\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{2}\right){\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{2}. $$

This has two consequences. First, by the lower bound above and the lower bound $\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\gtrsim 1$ ,

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)^{2}\gtrsim N|P_{11}|^{2}+N|P_{22}|^{2}+N|P_{12}|^{2}. $$

Thus, we can restrict the $P$ integration to $|P_{11}|+|P_{12}|+|P_{22}|\lesssim N^{-1/2}\log N$ at the cost of something exponentially small in $N$ . In particular, we have $\mathcal{E}=O(N^{-1/2+\kappa})$ for some $\kappa>0$ small. This bound on entries of $P$ combined with (4.3) also implies that

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}={\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}(P\otimes I_{N}) \displaystyle={\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}(P\otimes I_{N})+O\left(\frac{N^{2\kappa}}{\sqrt{N}\eta_{z,t}^{5}}\right). $$

Moreover, in the region $|P_{11}|+|P_{12}|+|P_{22}|\lesssim N^{-1/2}\log N$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{2}\lesssim\eta_{z,t}^{-C}\log^{2}N. $$

By combining this with (4.4), in this region, we have the following for $\kappa>0$ small:

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)^{2}={\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{2}+O\left(\frac{N^{\kappa}}{N\eta_{z,t}^{10}}\right). $$

Ultimately, for possibly different but still small $\kappa>0$ , we get

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{i}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{(rF)}}\right)^{2}+\mathcal{E}\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{i}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left(\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}(P\otimes I_{N})\sqrt{\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}}\right)^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{iO\left(\frac{N^{\kappa}}{\sqrt{N}\eta_{z,t}^{5}}\right)+O\left(\frac{N^{\kappa}}{N\eta_{z,t}^{10}}\right)\right\}. $$

Note that the second line above, which contains the main term on the RHS of this identity, is independent of $r$ . Thus, by the previous display, we have $m_{F}(r)\lesssim m_{F}(0)$ as long as $F$ is Hermitian and $\|\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}F\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\frac{N^{\epsilon}}{N\eta_{z,t}^{3}}\ll 1$ . Recalling that $m_{F}(0)=1$ , under this condition, we have $m_{F}(r)=O(1)$ . Concentration of matrix entries of $V_{1}^{\ast}G_{z}V_{1}$ now follows as Lemma 6.2 in [23]. In particular, we will apply this inequality for $r=N^{-\kappa}$ with $\kappa>0$ small and for the following choices of $F$ :

$$ \displaystyle F \displaystyle=\eta_{z,t}{\operatorname{Re}\,}\left[E\otimes H_{z}\right], \displaystyle F \displaystyle=\eta_{z,t}{\operatorname{Im}\,}\left[E\otimes H_{z}\right], \displaystyle F \displaystyle=\eta_{z,t}{\operatorname{Re}\,}\left[E\otimes\tilde{H}_{z}\right], \displaystyle F \displaystyle=\eta_{z,t}{\operatorname{Im}\,}\left[E\otimes\tilde{H}_{z}\right], \displaystyle F \displaystyle={\operatorname{Re}\,}\left[E\otimes H_{z}(A-z)\right], \displaystyle F \displaystyle={\operatorname{Im}\,}\left[E\otimes H_{z}(A-z)\right], $$

where $E$ is any of the four matrices

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\
0&0\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
0&0\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
1&0\end{pmatrix},\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&1\end{pmatrix}. $$

and ${\operatorname{Re}\,}X=\frac{1}{2}(X^{\ast}+X)$ , ${\operatorname{Im}\,}X=\frac{i}{2}(X^{\ast}-X)$ . (We note that our choice of $r$ is larger than the choices made in the proof of Lemma 6.2 in [23], giving weaker concentration estimates, but this is fine.) Let us illustrate one example. Upon treating $\mu_{j}$ as a probability measure over $\mathbf{v}$ , by the Markov inequality, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mu_{j}\left(\mathbf{v}^{\ast}F\mathbf{v}-\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}F\geq r\right)\leq e^{-Kr^{2}}m_{KF}(r). $$

Choose $F=\eta_{z,t}{\operatorname{Re}\,}\left[E\otimes H_{z}\right]$ and $r=N^{-\kappa}$ and $K=N^{3\kappa}$ for $\kappa>0$ small. Then we have the estimate $\|\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{rt}{N}KF\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1+2\kappa}\eta_{z,t}^{-3}\lesssim 1$ , so $m_{KF}(r)=O(1)$ . This shows that the event on the LHS is exponentially small in $\mu_{j}$ -measure. By the same token, we know the same is true if we replace $\geq r$ on the LHS by $\leq r$ , and we can replace ${\operatorname{Re}\,}[E\otimes H_{z}]$ by ${\operatorname{Im}\,}[E\otimes H_{z}]$ . For example, this implies $v_{1}^{\ast}H_{z}v_{1}=\frac{\eta_{z,t}t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}H_{z}+O(N^{-\kappa})$ outside an event of $\mu_{j}$ -probability that is exponentially small. Doing the same procedure for each entry of $V_{1}^{\ast}G_{z}V_{1}$ shows that each said entry matches the corresponding entry of $\mathcal{G}$ up to $O(N^{-\kappa})$ outside an event of $\mu_{j}$ -probability that is exponentially small. Since the determinant is smooth in its entries, and since the entries of $V_{1}^{\ast}G_{z}V_{1}$ are $O(\eta_{z,t}^{-1})=O(N^{-\epsilon_{0}})$ deterministically with $\epsilon_{0}>0$ small, we deduce

$$ \displaystyle\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}|\det[V_{1}^{\ast}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})V_{1}]|^{p}d\mu_{1}(\mathbf{v}_{1}) \displaystyle=|\det\mathcal{G}|^{p}+O(N^{-\kappa}). $$

We now claim that $|\det\mathcal{G}|^{p}\gtrsim\eta_{z,t}^{-D}$ for some $D=O(1)$ , since we can take $\eta_{z,t}=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ for $\epsilon_{0}>0$ small enough so that $\eta_{z,t}^{-D}\gg N^{-\kappa}$ . This implies that the RHS of the previous display is $|\det\mathcal{G}|^{p}[1+O(N^{-\kappa})]$ for possibly different $\kappa>0$ . But said claim is equivalent to $|\det[V_{1}^{\ast}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})V_{1}]|\gtrsim\eta_{z,t}^{-D}$ because of the previous display, and this bound is shown in the proof of Lemma 10. ∎

By the same argument, we deduce the following analog of Lemma 13 but for arbitrary $j\geq 1$ .

#### Lemma 14.

For any $p\geq 1$ and $j\geq 1$ , there exists $\kappa>0$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2j+2)}}|\det[V_{j}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(j-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{j}]|^{p}d\mu_{j}(\mathbf{v}_{j})=|\det\mathcal{G}_{j}|^{p}\left[1+O(N^{-\kappa})\right], $$

where $\mathcal{G}_{j}$ is the following $4\times 4$ matrix:

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},11}&\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},12}\\
\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},21}&\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},22}\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},11} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{11})&i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{12})\\
i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{21})&i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{22})\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},12} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[H_{z}^{(j-1)}(A^{(j-1)}-z)\otimes E_{11}]&\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[H_{z}^{(j-1)}(A^{(j-1)}-z)\otimes E_{12}]\\
\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[H_{z}^{(j-1)}(A^{(j-1)}-z)\otimes E_{21}]&\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[H_{z}^{(j-1)}(A^{(j-1)}-z)\otimes E_{22}]\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},21} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[(A^{(j-1)}-z)^{\ast}H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{11}]&\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[(A^{(j-1)}-z)^{\ast}H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{12}]\\
\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[(A^{(j-1)}-z)^{\ast}H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{21}]&\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}[(A^{(j-1)}-z)^{\ast}H_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{22}]\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j},22} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(\tilde{H}_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{11})&i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(\tilde{H}_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{12})\\
i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(\tilde{H}_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{21})&i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}(\tilde{H}_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{22})\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle E_{11} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\
0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad E_{22}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&1\end{pmatrix}\quad E_{12}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
0&0\end{pmatrix}\quad E_{21}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
1&0\end{pmatrix}. $$

The final step in this computation is to show that in $\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}$ , we can replace $a_{j},b_{j}$ by $a,b$ (i.e. replace $\lambda_{j}$ by $z$ ) and remove the $(j-1)$ -superscripts. For the exact formula for $\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}$ appearing in Lemma 15 below, see (4.11).

#### Lemma 15.

Define $\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}$ in the same way as in Lemma 14 but replacing $(a_{j},b_{j})$ by $(a,b)$ and $\theta_{j}$ by $\pi/4$ and removing the $(j-1)$ superscript. Then we have $|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}|^{p}=|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}|^{p}[1+O(N^{-\kappa})]$ for some $\kappa>0$ .

#### Proof.

Resolvent perturbation implies that $\|\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}-\tilde{H}_{a,b,\frac{\pi}{4}}^{(j-1)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\eta_{z,t}^{-C}[|a_{j}-a|+|b_{j}-b|+|\theta_{j}-\frac{\pi}{4}]$ . But $a_{j}-a,b_{j}-b=O(N^{-1/2})$ and $|\theta_{j}-\frac{\pi}{4}|=O(N^{-1/2+\kappa}\eta_{z,t}^{-1})$ . Moreover, if we use Cauchy interlacing as in (4.1), then for any $k,\ell\in\{1,2\}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle i\eta_{z,t}\frac{t}{N}\left|{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4}}^{(j-1)}(\tilde{H}_{z}^{(j-1)}\otimes E_{11})-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4}}(\tilde{H}_{z}\otimes E_{11})\right|\lesssim\tfrac{t}{N}\|\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|H_{z}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1}\eta_{z,t}^{-C}. $$

A similar estimate for removing $(j-1)$ -superscripts in entries of $\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}$ also holds. Thus, the entries of $\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}-\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}$ are $O(N^{-1/2+\kappa+C\epsilon_{0}})$ . Since the determinant is smooth in its entries, we deduce that $|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}|^{p}=|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}|^{p}+O(N^{-1/2+4\epsilon_{0}})$ . Now, again use the lower bound $|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}|^{p}\gtrsim\eta_{z,t}^{-D}$ for some $D=O(1)$ to get $|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a_{j},b_{j}}|^{p}\gtrsim\eta_{z,t}^{-D}$ . This implies that $|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}|^{p}+O(N^{-1/2+4\epsilon_{0}})=|\det\mathcal{G}_{j,a,b}|^{p}[1+O(N^{-1/2+4\epsilon_{0}})]$ and completes the proof. ∎

### 4.3 The $dP$ integration over $M_{2}^{sa}(\mathbb{R})$

We start by a similar computation to the $dP$ integration in the proof of Lemma 13. By $\det[1+A]=\exp{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log[1+A]$ and Taylor expansion of $\log$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\det[I+i[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}]^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{i}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left([\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}](P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{O(N\eta_{z,t}^{-6}\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{3})\right\}. $$

$$ \displaystyle\det[I+i[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}]^{-\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\lesssim\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left([\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}](P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\}. $$

If we write $P=\begin{pmatrix}P_{11}&P_{12}\\ P_{12}&P_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ , then an elementary computation shows

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left([\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}](P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\begin{pmatrix}P_{11}\\
P_{12}\\
P_{22}\end{pmatrix}^{\ast}\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}\begin{pmatrix}P_{11}\\
P_{12}\\
P_{22}\end{pmatrix}\right\}, $$

in which we use the notation

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}&\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},12}^{(j-1)}\\
\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},12}^{(j-1)}&\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},22}^{(j-1)}\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}[\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]_{1}&[\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]_{2}&[\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]_{3}\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle[\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]_{1} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}\\

We clarify that $\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix. To continue with this computation, we need the following auxiliary bound. (It is a refinement of (4.5).)

#### Lemma 16.

If $\theta\in\mathcal{I}_{0}$ , then $\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}\gtrsim N\eta_{z,t}^{-2}$ .

#### Proof.

This is shown for $\theta_{j}=\pi/4$ in Appendix B.1. For general $\theta_{j}\in\mathcal{I}_{0}$ , we will perform resolvent perturbation in the entries with respect to $\theta_{j}$ . We show one example; we claim that

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}={\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}+O(N^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}) $$

for $\delta>0$ small. For this, note $\|\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\eta_{z,t}^{-2}$ . Thus, resolvent perturbation shows

$$ \displaystyle\|[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}-[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\eta_{z,t}^{-D}\left\|(\Lambda_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}-\Lambda_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4}})\otimes I_{N-2j}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}} $$

for some $D=O(1)$ . Since $\theta\in\mathcal{I}_{0}$ , we know $\|\Lambda_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}-\Lambda_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim|\theta-\frac{\pi}{4}|\lesssim N^{-\frac{1}{2}+\tau}\eta_{z,t}^{-1}$ with $\tau>0$ small. So the RHS of the previous display is $\lesssim N^{-1/2+\tau}\eta_{z,t}^{-D}$ for different $D=O(1)$ and $\tau>0$ small. We deduce

$$ \displaystyle|{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}| \displaystyle\lesssim N\|[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}-[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4},11}^{(j-1)}]^{2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}+\tau}\eta_{z,t}^{-D} $$

at which point the claim follows if $\epsilon_{0}>0$ in $\eta_{z,t}=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ and $\tau>0$ are both small enough. A similar estimate holds for all entries of $\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}$ . This implies

$$ \displaystyle\|\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}-\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\frac{\pi}{4}}^{(j-1)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta} $$

with $\delta>0$ small. Since the lemma is true for $\theta_{j}=\pi/4$ as noted at the beginning of this proof, and since $N\eta_{z,t}^{-2}\gg N^{1/2+\delta}$ for $\delta>0$ small, the lemma must be true for all $\theta_{j}\in\mathcal{I}_{0}$ . ∎

By Lemma 16 and (4.7), we deduce the following for any $\upsilon>0$

$$ \displaystyle\left|\int_{\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\geq N^{-\frac{1}{2}+\upsilon}\eta_{z,t}}e^{i\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}P}\det[I+i[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}(P\otimes I)[\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{(j-1)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}]^{-\frac{1}{2}}dP\right|\lesssim\exp[-CN^{2\upsilon}]. $$

In particular, we can restrict to the region $\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq N^{-1/2+\upsilon}\eta_{z,t}$ . In this region, we can use the identity (4.6) and control the last line therein (the cubic term) by $N^{-1/2+3\tau}$ for $\tau>0$ small. In particular, we have

A similar argument lets us extend the integration back to all $M_{2}^{sa}(\mathbb{R})$ . We ultimately have

P_{12}\\
P_{22}\end{pmatrix}\right\}dP+O(\exp[-CN^{2\upsilon}]). $$

We can compute the $dP$ integration above since it is just a Gaussian Fourier transform; this gives

-2{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},12}^{(j-1)}\\

\frac{N}{t}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},22}^{(j-1)}\end{pmatrix}\right\|\lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}+\kappa}\eta_{z,t}^{-D}, $$

### 4.4 Putting it altogether

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{\mathrm{main}}(z,\mathbf{z};A)=\frac{16N^{7}b^{4}[1+O(N^{-\kappa})]}{\pi^{4}t^{12}\gamma_{z,t}^{2}\sigma_{z,t}^{3}\upsilon_{z,t}^{2}}\rho_{\mathrm{GinUE}}^{(2)}(z_{1},z_{2})\int_{\mathcal{I}_{0}^{2}}d\theta_{1}d\theta_{2}\frac{|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{\sin^{2}\theta_{1}\sin^{2}\theta_{2}} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,2}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2j+2})}d\mu_{j}(\mathbf{v}_{j})|\det[V_{j}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(j-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{j}]|^{j} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-b_{j}^{2}(\tan\theta_{j}-\tan^{-1}\theta_{j})^{2}\eta_{z,t}^{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}H_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\lambda}_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})\right\} \displaystyle\times\mathbf{C}_{1}|\det\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}|^{-\frac{1}{2}}\exp\left\{-\mathbf{C}_{2}\begin{pmatrix}\frac{N}{t}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}\\
-2{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},12}\\
\frac{N}{t}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},22}\end{pmatrix}^{\ast}\mathbf{Q}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j}}^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}\frac{N}{t}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},11}\\
-2{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},12}\\
\frac{N}{t}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{a_{j},b_{j},\theta_{j},22}\end{pmatrix}\right\} \displaystyle+O(\exp[-CN^{\kappa}]). $$

By (2.47), Proposition 8, and our computation of the remaining $4\times 4$ determinants (see Lemmas 14 and 15), we deduce
